title: ENDEX: 2:00 PM PDT, Final Sitrep and No Return Order

fields.resolution: ENDEX. It is now 14:00 PDT, 3 hours 46 minutes after the earthquake, and Command reads the final sitrep: the mainshock is M 9.0 (USGS Event Summary version 3, REVIEWED), and NTWC has downgraded the coast to a Tsunami Advisory, Message Number 7, issued 13:44, with the Port Alder gauge at +0.6 m at 13:38 (observed). The return criteria are NOT met because NTWC has not cancelled and the gauge has not stayed below 0.3 m for two hours, so no return order has been issued and the XL and XXL zones, the harbor and the Alder River flats remain evacuated. This concludes the exercise. EXERCISE EXERCISE EXERCISE.
finalState: EARTHQUAKE: M 9.0 (v3, reviewed; first automatic estimates M 7.3 ShakeAlert, M 8.0 NTWC preliminary). Largest aftershock M 7.5 (reviewed) at 11:52; M 5.4 (automatic) at 13:31. ShakeMap and PAGER (RED) are modeled estimates and are reported separately from field observations.
ROUTES: Highway 101 Alder River bridge CLOSED pending inspection by an ODOT bridge engineer, with a 300 ft gas exclusion zone. Highway 6 Neskin grade CLOSED at about MP 9 (landslide).

PLACARDS: 911 backup positions INSPECTED (green); Marlow Coast High School INSPECTED (green), but the shelter is at capacity and the generator is out; Kellerton Fire Station 3 RESTRICTED USE (yellow). The hospital and the Front Street masonry are NOT YET INSPECTED, and teams are staged at the XXL line until the return order.
POWER: Cape Marlow PUD has restored about 1,200 of 14,500 meters (Kellerton feeder). Substations 2 and 3 have no estimate.

EARLY WARNING ACTION LOG: ShakeAlert 10:14:02; Station 1 doors 10:14:05; Station 2 doors 10:14:06; Station 3 doors opened manually 10:16 (confirmed late); hospital elevator recall confirmed 10:24; school bell 10:14:12; sirens 10:17:05 (3 of 18 silent); 911 transfer to backup complete 10:52.
fields.hotWashTransition: Thank you, everyone. Play has stopped. Put down your phones, radios and status boards and leave your logs and message drafts where they are. We will take a ten-minute break and then start the hot wash in this room.
fields.hotWashMethod: Timeline walk-back with 3-Up, 3-Down: we replay the Early Warning Action Log and each decision time against the clock, then each role names three things that worked and three things that broke.
hotWashQuestions: We acted on shaking before the 10:19 Tsunami Warning arrived. Where did we wait for a message, and what did that cost in minutes for Cedar Court, the harbor and the Port Alder 911 center?

We went from M 7.3 to M 8.0, M 8.9 and then M 9.0. Did the PIO, the 911 caller script and the WebEOC board ever quote the same magnitude, version number and zone names at the same time? Where did they drift apart?
Who could not leave on their own (Cedar Court wheelchair users, the hospital's non-ambulatory patients, the ten unreunified students), and when did each of them actually reach safe ground?
With rumors, a TV chyron and a downgrade to Advisory all saying it was over, what held the evacuation? Who owns the return order, and are our criteria written down?
How did we explain that a green placard and the aftershock forecast are different things, and that a green placard is not a guarantee against a 30 percent chance of an M 7 or larger this week?
fields.facilitatorNote: Collect every log, message draft, WebEOC printout and evaluator sheet before the break. Flag any player who issued or implied a return or all-clear during play, and note the late Station 3 door and hospital elevator confirmations for the after-action report.
fields.scenarioTitle: The Second Wave: Cascadia Rupture, Tsunami Evacuation & Message Discipline

instructorNote: This card ends play. Command should confirm the sitrep and say that the return criteria are still open before the room breaks for the hot wash. Watch for anyone who treats the downgrade to Advisory as an all-clear. That is a key hot wash point, because only the county can give the local return order.
